name: A02YYUW waterproof ultrasonic distance sensor (UART)
description: Sealed IP67 ultrasonic distance sensor (3–450 cm, ±1 cm, 3 cm blind zone, 60° beam) for tank levels and outdoor use. Runs on 3.3–5 V and sends a 4-byte frame by itself about every 100 ms at 9600 baud: 0xFF, distance high byte, distance low byte, checksum (low 8 bits of the sum of the first three); distance is in mm. Leave RX floating or high for the smoothed (processed) value, pull it low for the real-time value. Sold as: DFRobot A02YYUW Waterproof Ultrasonic Sensor (SEN0311, UART version), 4-wire PH2.0 cable VCC, GND, RX, TX.
eli5: A waterproof sound-echo sensor: it chirps, times the echo, and keeps telling your board how far away the water or object is, in millimetres, over a serial wire.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.3–5 V (pin 1, red wire); TX logic follows VCC, so use 3.3 V on ESP32/Pico

pins.name: RX
pins.description: Output mode select, sensor input (pin 3, yellow wire): floating or high = processed (smoothed) value, low = real-time value. May be wired to the board's UART TX, which idles high

pins.name: TX
pins.description: Sensor serial output, 9600 baud 8-N-1 (pin 4, white wire): wire to the board's UART RX

supplierQuery: DFRobot A02YYUW SEN0311 waterproof ultrasonic sensor UART
buildNotes: The sensor talks first: no command is needed. Each frame is 0xFF, DATA_H, DATA_L, SUM with SUM = (0xFF + DATA_H + DATA_L) & 0xFF; distance mm = DATA_H × 256 + DATA_L.

Wire the sensor's TX (white) to the board's UART RX. RX (yellow) only selects the output mode: floating or high gives the processed value (steadier, 100–300 ms response), low gives the real-time value (100 ms).
Power it from 3.3 V on ESP32 / Pico so its TX stays at 3.3 V logic; at 5 V it outputs 5 V levels.
Readings below 30 mm (blind zone) or above 4500 mm are not reliable; the beam is 60° wide, so keep the sensor away from tank walls.
IP67 means it survives splashes and condensation; it measures through air, not underwater. Leave at least 3 cm between the sensor face and the highest water level.
Frames pile up in the UART buffer while the program sleeps: flush before reading so you get the current distance, and check the checksum.

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from a02yyuw import A02YYUW

# board TX -> sensor RX (idles high = processed-value mode), board RX <- sensor TX
uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RX}), rx=Pin({TX}))
sensor = A02YYUW(uart)
while True:
    d = sensor.distance_mm()
    if d is None:
        print('no reading')
    else:
        print('D=%dmm' % d)
    time.sleep_ms(500)
